title: Scalable emulation of protein equilibrium ensembles with generative deep learning

nodes.text: BioEmu (Biomolecular Emulator) is a generative deep learning system that samples thousands of statistically independent structures from a protein's approximate equilibrium ensemble per hour on a single GPU, using an AlphaFold2 evoformer sequence encoder feeding a denoising diffusion model over coarse-grained backbone frames.
nodes.evidence: we develop a Biomolecular Emulator (BioEmu), a generative deep learning system that can generate thousands of statistically independent samples from the protein structure ensemble per hour on a single graphical processing unit

nodes.text: BioEmu uses a similar model architecture to Distributional Graphormer but employs a significantly different training approach.
nodes.evidence: BioEmu uses a similar model architecture as Distributional Graphormer [13], but with a significantly different training approach

nodes.text: BioEmu is trained by combining heterogeneous data: a clustered AlphaFold database (AFDB) for pretraining with a multi-structure augmentation strategy, over 200 milliseconds of all-atom MD reweighted toward equilibrium (via Markov State Models or experimental weights), and ~750K experimental protein stability measurements from MEGAscale.
nodes.evidence: over 200 milliseconds of MD simulation, and experimental protein stabilities ... 750 K exp. protein stabilities

nodes.text: Property-prediction fine-tuning (PPFT) is a new algorithm that incorporates experimental protein stability measurements (which lack structures) directly into diffusion model training.
nodes.evidence: we developed an new algorithm called property-prediction fine-tuning (PPFT) to efficiently incorporate experimental measurements into diffusion model training

nodes.text: Prior generative ML systems have mainly demonstrated qualitative sampling of distinct conformational states; BioEmu aims to be the first to quantitatively match equilibrium ensembles and predict experimental observables.
nodes.evidence: generative ML systems have mainly demonstrated an ability to qualitatively sample distinct protein conformational states. A demonstration that generative ML can quantitatively match equilibrium ensembles ... is critical going forward

nodes.text: Unlike Boltzmann Generators, which can efficiently sample arbitrary equilibrium distributions but are difficult to scale to large proteins, BioEmu is designed to scale.
nodes.evidence: Boltzmann Generators [12] (BGs), which can efficiently sample arbitrarily-defined equilibrium distributions ... but are difficult to scale to large proteins

nodes.text: BioEmu samples protein conformations with relative free energy errors around 1 kcal/mol, validated against millisecond-timescale MD and experimentally-measured protein stabilities, on the order of experimental accuracy.
nodes.evidence: BioEmu samples protein conformations with relative free energy errors around 1 kcal/mol

nodes.text: On the challenging OOD60 test set (19 proteins with strict sequence-similarity limits), BioEmu significantly outperforms AFCluster and AlphaFlow at sampling conformational changes.
nodes.evidence: our model significantly outperforms the two considered baseline approaches (Fig. S5a)

nodes.text: BioEmu predicts 85% of reference experimental structures within 3 Angstrom RMSD, capturing large-scale domain motions, local unfolding, and cryptic pocket formation.
nodes.evidence: BioEmu predicts 85% of the reference experimental structures with ≤3 Å RMSD

nodes.text: BioEmu's performance is similar for proteins overlapping versus not overlapping the AlphaFold2 training set, indicating it does not trivially extract capabilities from evoformer embeddings.
nodes.evidence: the model's performance is similar for proteins that overlap with the AlphaFold2 training set and those that do not, indicating that the benchmark does not test capabilities that the model trivially extracted from evoformer embeddings

nodes.text: Using a second-order integration scheme, BioEmu generates structures in as few as 100 denoising steps with sequence encoding invoked only once per protein, sampling 10,000 independent structures within minutes to a few hours on one GPU.
nodes.evidence: using a second-order integration scheme we generate protein structures in as few as 100 denoising steps ... 10,000 independent protein structures ... within minutes to a few hours on a single GPU

nodes.text: By simultaneously emulating structural ensembles and thermodynamic properties, BioEmu reveals mechanistic insights such as the causes of fold destabilization in mutants, and the prediction error decreases with more diverse training data.
nodes.evidence: the prediction error decreases with an increasing amount of diverse training data indicates a path forward for predicting biomolecular function at genomic scale
